Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and for flagging the procurement timeline. I hear you that Acme needs a path to recover royalties and certain IP-related awards outside the general cap.

To move quickly, here are two pragmatic options we can propose to Acme:

1) Narrow IP-remedy carve-out: Exclude from the monetary cap only third-party liability that arises from a final adjudication or settlement for IP infringement and expressly allow recovery of reasonable royalties and court-ordered remedies. This keeps the carve-out limited to adjudicated infringement claims.

2) Mitigation-first approach: Keep the cap but allow recovery of royalties and reasonable out-of-pocket amounts if Acme first pursues reasonable mitigation (e.g., license procurement or replacement). This limits exposure while addressing Acme's concern.

Marissa — can you draft a short redline for option #1 (preferred from sales) that we can send to Acme today? Karthik, FYI on timing — finance may need to sign off if we remove exposure from the cap entirely.

I attached a one-page summary of the two options (redlines_highlighted.pdf). Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Ben / Karthik / Sarah — see proposed redline below (inline) for a narrowly-tailored exclusion that protects Redwood while addressing Acme's commercial ask. My comments follow the language.

----- PROPOSED ORDER FORM LANGUAGE (redline) -----

"Notwithstanding Section 12 (Limitation of Liability), the monetary cap shall not apply to amounts finally awarded by a court or agreed in settlement to which Customer is entitled arising from claims of third-party infringement of Customer's intellectual property, provided that (a) Customer has notified Provider promptly of the claim; (b) Provider is given sole control of the defense or, if Provider declines control, Customer elects to settle only to the extent necessary to avoid an injunction; and (c) any recovery for past use shall be limited to reasonable royalties as determined by the court or mutually agreed settlement."

Key points / risk notes:
- "Finally awarded or agreed in settlement" narrows scope to mature claims; avoids open-ended exposure for mere allegations.
- We retain ability to control defense which reduces Redwood's litigation exposure.
- We limited recoverable amounts to "reasonable royalties" for past use rather than unlimited punitive or consequential amounts.

If Acme insists on unfettered removal of the cap for IP claims, I recommend we tie that to procurement of IP insurance or an express indemnity with limits.

If this looks good to you Ben, I'll insert the redline into the Order Form and circulate a clean copy to Acme with a short explanatory email.
